features/calendar.manual: Calendar and activity drafts, recurrence and page design use explicit grants and current versions. Publishing requires calendar:publish and an explicit request. Archive/restore of published items, subscription and delivery settings, and external feeds require the calendar workspace; native publication can trigger subscriber updates.

features/cms.manual: Page copies, languages, revision restoration and draft menus/appearance require explicit management/settings grants. Publishing exact saved content or settings needs website:publish and an explicit request. Menu-only publication preserves published appearance. Timed publication, deleting, template installation, private-media visibility and executable code require staff workflows.

features/events.manual: Publishing saved event details or editorial prizes needs events:publish and an explicit request; existing page, public-media, domain permission and recent-authentication checks apply. Packages, teams, participant records, payments, entries, draws and cancellation require staff workflows. Only recent cookie-authenticated staff can apply operational settings proposals.

features/forms.manual: Publishing saved forms needs forms:publish, an explicit request and current form/event publisher authority. Responses, export, deletion, recipients and webhooks remain outside automation.

features/guests.manual: Guest identities, access grants and purchases are private participant workflows, not website content.

features/media.manual: New uploads are private. Image pixels need an explicit inspection scope. Public visibility and deletion remain manual.

features/members.manual: Member accounts, applications, approvals and access changes are human-controlled private workflows.

features/partners.manual: Publishing saved profiles needs directory:publish and an explicit request; images must already be public. Restoration and contacting partners remain manual.

integrations/automation.manual: REST API and MCP have separate disabled-by-default switches, workspaces, documentation and credentials. REST keys cannot authorize MCP and MCP keys/OAuth cannot authorize REST. Staff register clients and approve actions; existing grants never widen automatically. Optional renewal and remembered consent avoid routine reapproval while current session and permission checks remain. New grants require recent sign-in. Publication needs an explicit grant, current authority, saved version and user request. Transport switches and applying operational proposals are never tools.

integrations/email.manual: Provider credentials, templates, recipients and real delivery require staff configuration.

integrations/google.manual: Provider credentials, domain policy and Google session verification require staff configuration. Platform-wide login policy and appearance are human-managed Settings; REST and MCP never change authentication policy.

integrations/luma.manual: Provider credentials, synchronization, participant data and purchases require approved provider workflows.

integrations/ui.manual: Presentation of integration settings; has no separate automation action.

core.manual: Identity is readable through website_context; installation, ownership, memberships, domains, settings and feature switches remain manual.

infrastructure.manual: Storage, databases, encryption and delivery adapters have no direct automation interface.

composition.manual: Composition wires shared services into REST and MCP; it must not bypass service authorization.

app/api.manual: Legacy cookie APIs remain staff workflows. Only explicitly registered v1 operations are callable through automation.

../db/schema.manual: Schema changes require review of DTOs, migrations, scopes and both automation interfaces.

app/automation-preview.manual: One-use internal rendering only. Scripts and external requests are blocked; saved private media requires explicit inspection authority.
